title: The system: concert ticketing on sale day, where demand outruns checkout
caption: Each layer has a limit and a policy for when it's reached: wait at the edge, reject fast at the API, and never queue more than the workers can finish in time.

steps.text: Sale opens at 10:00 and a million fans arrive within a minute. The event page is static and served from the edge, so browsing costs the core nothing.
Above the core's capacity the edge sends new arrivals to the waiting room: a FIFO line that shows each fan a position and an ETA.
The room admits fans at the rate the core can take, handing each a signed token. That rate is not fixed: it comes from live load signals.
The Checkout API admits a request only if it holds a token and the order queue has room; otherwise it answers 503 with Retry-After in about a millisecond.
Accepted orders go into a bounded queue (about 20 s of work). Workers pull at their own pace, hold seats and charge the card.
Queue depth and age feed back: they slow the waiting room and raise the shed level. Optional work goes first: recommendations are skipped and emails deferred.

scenarios.name: On-sale spike
scenarios.summary: 100× the normal traffic, and the core sees a steady stream: the crowd waits in the cheapest place, at the edge.

steps.text: Arrivals jump to 100× what checkout can process.
Almost all of them wait in the room. A fan in the line costs a cached page and a poll every 10 s.
Admission stays at 3 000 per minute, so the order queue hovers well below its bound.
Workers run at full speed, but never beyond it.

scenarios.name: Payment provider slows
scenarios.summary: A slow dependency fills the bounded queue; the full queue turns into fast rejections and a slower line instead of a crash.

steps.text: Payment latency goes from 300 ms to 3 s. Each worker slot is busy 10× longer.
Workers pull less, so the queue fills: 2 000 orders in under a minute.
At the bound, the API rejects new orders with 503 + Retry-After. Nothing is queued that would time out anyway.
The signals lower the admit rate, the room's ETA goes up, and fans see an honest wait instead of a spinner. When payment recovers, the rate rises again.

scenarios.name: Risk: raise the bound
scenarios.summary: Raising the queue limit to stop the 503s only moves the failure: the work outlives its callers. Tune the admit rate, not the buffer.

steps.text: An operator raises the order queue's bound from 2 000 to 50 000 to make the 503s go away.
The queue now holds about 8 minutes of work. Clients time out after 30 s and retry, adding more orders.
Workers process orders whose buyers have already left; their seats sit in holds that nobody pays for.
Fix: restore the bound, drop orders older than the client deadline before working on them, and let the waiting room absorb the crowd.
